first.rationale: Three inherited memories (31, 86, 91) all touch overlapping onboarding/activation territory, and two of them (86, 91) are due for consolidation-driven confirmation given the current 4-6% declines in exactly those metrics. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the most tempting lever given the competitor's pricing attack, but it is also the most consequential for the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue: a price-matching response risks attracting the same price-sensitive churn-prone segment the competitor is fighting for, and the original record needs checking for revenue quality and retention effects, not just acquisition lift. I'm spending verification budget on memory_73 (highest stakes, least aligned with 'sustainable qualified revenue') and memory_86 (most directly relevant to the current onboarding-completion drop, and overlapping/redundant with memory_31, so worth confirming which is the stronger original result). Pending that check, I intend a small guarded onboarding-simplification test rather than a pricing response, since chasing the competitor on price is reversible-in-theory but reputationally and margin-wise risky if the underlying memory doesn't hold up, whereas onboarding fixes are lower-risk and address a metric that's declining regardless of competitive dynamics.

final.rationale: Verification confirmed the risk: exp_73 shows targeted discounting drove +18% qualified revenue but -12% 30-day retention, meaning the acquired cohort likely fails to survive renewal — directly contradicting the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is now explicitly ruled out despite competitive pressure; matching the competitor's price attack would likely just harvest another short-lived low-quality cohort. Exp_86 confirmed with positive retention (+3%) alongside completion and time-to-value gains, and it directly targets the current 4% onboarding-completion decline while also plausibly helping the 6% activation decline (consistent with memory_31's overlapping, unverified but directionally consistent claim). Given confirmed evidence, positive retention signal, and direct relevance to two of the three current problems, I'm committing this week's single experiment slot to onboarding simplification, scaled as a standard experiment (not just a guarded test) since the underlying mechanism is now source-verified rather than merely inherited. I'm still flagging downstream_value_risk because retention lift was measured at 30 days only, not over a full renewal cycle, so long-term revenue quality should be monitored rather than assumed durable.
